ORBIT / A STUDY OF MOTIONStory & share ↗↓ Offline HTML
HOW IT WORKS

Circles become a drawing.

Orbit samples a closed path at 8,192 evenly spaced points and decomposes it using a fast Fourier transform. Each rotating circle represents a frequency component.

In X · Y mode, the horizontal position of the top chain and the vertical position of the left chain meet at the drawing point. Choose 1–5,000 signed-frequency terms, ordered from low to high frequency. Each axis uses N terms; with even N, the last frequency pair is incomplete.

Image lab offers automatic silhouette detection, transparency extraction, adaptive thresholding and Canny-style edges. Denoise, morphological cleanup, area filtering, simplification and smoothing refine the result. These are geometric image-processing tools, not semantic AI segmentation. Photo-edge mode traces boundaries of edge regions, which can produce double outlines.

The error compares the Fourier reconstruction against the selected, processed path, not against the original photo. PNG exports the current canvas. SVG exports the complete reconstructed path. Video export records one loop in portrait, square or landscape format. MP4 is offered when supported; otherwise choose WebM. Keep the page visible until export finishes. Project JSON stores the active path and drawing, not the original image or image-lab settings.
